title: Chat UX pass, 46 turns in 13 conversations through the real route and tools
passRule: German replies stay German, a reply follows the language of the latest message after a switch (a message with no own words keeps the language the user types in, a request for a language holds), replies stay within 3 sentences, offer_screening_answers is called with a start-screening-flow chip exactly when the form questions come up, no document count or score the model was not given, and the compaction summary keeps its copied ad lines in German.
decisionRule:
Per site, pick the lowest-effort Haiku arm (order: low-nothink, low, medium, high) that satisfies ALL of:
1. Primary metric: its case failures are at most one more than the best Haiku arm (counting every case of every run). The 95% Wilson intervals are reported but do not qualify an arm (tightened before any paid run, 2026-10-22: at these sample sizes overlapping intervals admit several extra failures).
2. Hard constraints: for every hard-constraint metric it has no more violations than the gpt-oss arm, and zero violations for the metrics a site lists as absolute (ranking: hard-constraint violations in the top 10 must be 0, and hard_in_surfaced (every surfaced item) is held to the gpt-oss count; language: any fallback to English fails the case and is a hard violation under 'fallback', on every document, English included, held to the gpt-oss count; every site: no call over the 100k input budget). Runs graded before that language change (2026-10-22, commit d5b829e5) counted only 'fallback_on_non_english' (a fallback on a non-English document), so their language hard counts are not comparable with later runs.
3. It produced no errors (a thrown error, an empty reply, a budget stop) that the best Haiku arm did not also produce.
Tie-break between arms of the same effort rank: lower p50 per-call latency. If no arm qualifies the site is undecided and the orchestrator decides by hand.
A run that aborted (the --max-cost stop) or whose arms ran unequal case counts is undecided, whatever the numbers (added 2026-10-22 after review: an arm cut short has fewer chances to fail).
gpt-oss is a baseline only: it is never a candidate. A winner with more primary failures than gpt-oss is flagged for the orchestrator. Cache hit rate and cost are reported but do not enter the rule.
